result.title: Density-Guided Bootstrap Boundaries for Latent World-Model Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Latent world models allow reinforcement learning agents to learn policies from imagined trajectories, yet determining the optimal depth of model reliance remains a fundamental challenge. Fixed imagination horizons apply uniform prediction depths regardless of trajectory reliability, exposing target values to compounding model error or over-relying on critic approximations. We introduce density-guided bootstrap boundaries, a trajectory-dependent mechanism that adapts the depth of imagined returns using a score-informed relative density proxy. The proxy accumulates the estimated divergence of a score-corrected auxiliary field formed by a feature displacement network and a noise-conditioned score estimator along imagined paths. We propose two gating mechanisms: a hard boundary that halts return expansion at a discrete state, and a soft boundary that continuously shifts the return recursion toward critic bootstrapping. Both variants preserve boundary value estimates and apply corresponding survival weights to actor and critic losses. Formulated independently of specific dynamics models and instantiated within Dreamer V3, we prove that the resulting gated Bellman operator is a strict contraction mapping and that early bootstrapping monotonically reduces conditional target variance. We clarify the theoretical assumptions distinguishing our expansion proxy from exact path likelihoods. Across continuous-control tasks and Atari Pong, empirical evaluations show that dynamic boundary selection enhances sample efficiency and late-training performance over fixed-horizon and auxiliary-enabled baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Dreamer V3 中提出「密度引导的 bootstrap 边界」：用一个由特征位移网络与噪声条件 score 估计器构成的辅助场，沿想象轨迹累积其散度作为相对密度代理，自适应决定回报展开深度，并给出硬截断与软过渡两种门控及收缩性、方差下降的理论结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 以轨迹可靠性信号动态决定 latent 想象展开到何处为止，可能与 LVR 中「STOP」决策、按证据可信度截断推理深度以及 latent 轨迹可信度估计存在概念联系，但属世界模型 RL 场景，可迁移性有待核查。
